## Rent Problem In NY! (Final Project Idea)

*Rent is one of our biggest everyday concerns, and in New York, prices have been climbing steadily since 2020 often feeling like they're hitting the ceiling. What's striking is that even with rents this high, popular neighborhoods like Williamsburg, Greenpoint, and the West Village still have very few vacant apartments. That combination of high prices and extremely low vacancy makes this an especially compelling topic for our project: it's a real world case study in how supply and demand actually plays out in the housing market. If you are interested hit yes :) and please check below I've put medians of rent prices In NYC borough map*

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(leaflet)

boroughs <- data.frame(
  name = c("Manhattan", "Brooklyn", "Queens", "The Bronx", "Staten Island"),
  lat  = c(40.7831, 40.6782, 40.7282, 40.8448, 40.5795),
  lng  = c(-73.9712, -73.9442, -73.7949, -73.8648, -74.1502),
  median_rent = c(5117, 4054, 3561, 3171, 2200)
)

pal <- colorNumeric(palette = "YlOrRd", domain = boroughs$median_rent)

leaflet(boroughs) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>
  setView(lng = -73.95, lat = 40.71, zoom = 10) |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~lng, lat = ~lat,
    radius = ~median_rent / 250,
    color = ~pal(median_rent),
    fillOpacity = 0.8,
    stroke = FALSE,
    label = ~paste0(name, ": $", format(median_rent, big.mark = ","), "/mo"),
    labelOptions = labelOptions(noHide = FALSE, direction = "top")
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    pal = pal, values = ~median_rent,
    title = "Median Rent",
    labFormat = labelFormat(prefix = "$")
  )
```

*Median asking rent by NYC borough (larger, darker circles = higher rent). Hover over a marker to see the exact figure.*
